A sandstone chapel carved into the hillside

bank.prompt: Fortitude Valley got its name from a ship that arrived in Brisbane in 1849. What was that ship called?
bank.reveal: Scottish immigrants aboard the barque Fortitude arrived at Brisbane in January 1849. Denied promised free land, they camped nearby — and named the area after their ship.

source.title: Fortitude Valley | Queensland Places
source.publisher: Centre for the Government of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The first vessel, the Fortitude, arrived at Brisbane in January 1849' and 'The temporary abode gave rise to the name Fortitude Valley.'

bank.prompt: The suburb name 'Indooroopilly' comes from an Aboriginal word. What does it mean?
bank.reveal: Brisbane City Council's Heritage Trail explains the name comes from an Aboriginal word believed to mean a gully or creek with leeches — a nod to the leech-filled gullies once running to the Brisbane River.

source.title: Indooroopilly Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The name Indooroopilly is thought to come from an Aboriginal word. It is believed to mean a gully or creek with leeches.'

bank.prompt: Which came first at the site of Toohey Forest Park — the Toohey family settling their cattle property, or the Commonwealth acquiring part of the land for a post-war Soldiers Settlement?

options.label: The Toohey family settling Mount Galway

bank.reveal: The Toohey family occupied 'Mount Galway' from 1872. The Commonwealth only acquired the first section of the park in 1919, for a proposed WWI Soldiers Settlement.

source.title: Toohey Forest Park | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'the Toohey family from 1872 to 1946' and 'The Commonwealth acquired the first section of the park in 1919 for a proposed post World War 1 Soldiers Settlement.'

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Teneriffe got its unusual name from a landowner in the 1850s. What did he name it after?

options.label: The largest of the Canary Islands
A Scottish coastal village he grew up near

bank.reveal: Property speculator James Gibbon named his 1854 land holding after Tenerife, the largest island in the Canary Islands archipelago — giving the suburb its distinctive double-F spelling.

source.title: 46 Kingsholme Street, Teneriffe | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'Gibbon's naming of Teneriffe was a variation of Tenerife, the largest island in the Canary Islands archipelago.'

bank.prompt: The heritage cottages at Cairns Street, Kangaroo Point were built in the 1880s as what type of housing?
bank.reveal: A 1880s Brisbane building boom drove the Kangaroo Point population from 1,903 to 3,204 in just five years. Landowner Mullen built the Cairns Street cottages specifically as rental properties for workers, many employed at Moar's nearby shipyard.

source.title: 35 Cairns Street, Kangaroo Point | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states the cottages are 'purpose-built nineteenth century rental cottages' and that 'landowners like Mullen constructed rental houses on their properties' to meet the 1880s housing demand.

bank.prompt: George Hellicar, who co-owned the heritage-listed 'Waratah' flats in Woolloongabba, was a foundation member of the Queensland Law Society. What role was he appointed to at its formation in 1873?
bank.reveal: Hellicar was 'appointed as honorary secretary' when the Queensland Law Society was formed at the Supreme Court in Brisbane in August 1873.

source.title: Waratah | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states Hellicar 'was one of the foundation members of the Queensland Law Society when it was formed at the Supreme Court in Brisbane in August 1873' and 'Appointed as honorary secretary'.

bank.prompt: Toohey Forest Park occupies land that was once a cattle grazing property owned by the Toohey family from the 1870s. What was that property called?
bank.reveal: The park's site was the cattle grazing property 'Mount Galway', home of the Toohey family from 1872 to 1946, before Brisbane City Council completed its purchase and declared it parkland.

source.title: Toohey Forest Park | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The Park's site was part of the cattle grazing property 'Mount Galway' that was the home of district pioneers, the Toohey family from 1872 to 1946.'

bank.prompt: Which came first — the formation of the Greater Brisbane Council, or the opening of Brisbane City Hall?

options.label: The formation of the Greater Brisbane Council
The opening of Brisbane City Hall

bank.reveal: Greater Brisbane Council was formed on 1 October 1925 when 20 local authorities amalgamated. City Hall didn't open until April 1930 — five years later.

source.title: Council history | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'On 1 October 1925, the greater Brisbane Council came into effect' and 'Council started meeting in the Brisbane City Hall in 1928 while construction was being completed, before opening in April 1930.'

bank.prompt: Which came first — the opening of Brisbane City Hall, or the opening of the Story Bridge?

options.label: The opening of Brisbane City Hall
The opening of the Story Bridge

bank.reveal: Brisbane City Hall opened in April 1930. The Story Bridge didn't open until 1940, a full decade later, when cross-river bus services also commenced.

source.title: Council history | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states City Hall opened in April 1930 and 'Cross river bus services commenced in 1940, with the opening of the Story Bridge.'

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Albion takes its name from a hotel built in 1864. What inspired the hotel's name?

options.label: White quarry walls that reminded the owner of England's white cliffs
A famous inn of the same name in London's East End

bank.reveal: The original Albion Hotel's owner, Tom Haselden, saw the white stone quarry walls nearby and was reminded of the white cliffs of Dover — so the suburb inherited a name rooted in a local landmark.

source.title: Albion Hotel | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The suburb of Albion was named after the hotel' and that Haselden named it because 'the white walls of the stone quarry in the area reminded him of the white cliffs of Dover.'

bank.prompt: The heritage-listed Spilsbury's Cottage in Spring Hill (built 1865–72) sat on the slopes, not the ridges. According to its heritage register entry, who lived on Spring Hill's ridges versus its slopes?

options.label: Wealthy on ridges; middle-class tradesmen on slopes
Working-class labourers on ridges; wealthy on slopes

bank.reveal: Ridge roads with cooling breezes attracted wealthier residents, while middle-class grocers, clerks and skilled tradesmen — like the Spilsburys — lived on Spring Hill's slopes.

source.title: Spilsbury's Cottage - Brisbane Heritage Register
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Those with the means to own the highest land with cooling breezes and expansive views built residences along the ridges, while the middle classes of shopkeepers and artisans lived on the slopes of Spring Hill'.

bank.prompt: What form of public transport first connected Albion to the city in 1882, opening up the suburb to rapid growth?
bank.reveal: The Roma Street–Sandgate railway opened in 1882, making Albion a popular suburb. The tramline linking Albion with Clayfield and the city didn't open until 1899.

source.title: Albion Public Hall (former) | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'the coming of the railway in 1882 saw the urbanisation of the area' and 'in 1899 a tramline linking Albion with Clayfield and the city opened'

bank.prompt: The former Ascot fire station on Racecourse Road was built in 1920 but closed just seven years later. What purpose did it serve during World War Two?
bank.reveal: After closing in 1927 when a new station opened at Albion, the building served as offices for the Allied Forces during World War Two, then later as tertiary education and community facilities.

source.title: Ascot Fire Station (former) | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states it was used as 'offices for the Allied Forces during World War Two' after closing as a fire station in 1927

bank.prompt: The grand hilltop mansion Whytecliffe in Albion was built in 1876 for which notable Queensland official?
bank.reveal: Whytecliffe was designed by architect F.D.G. Stanley and built in 1876 as an elite private residence for Robert Little, Queensland's Crown Solicitor. It later became part of St Columban's College.

source.title: St Columban's Christian Brothers College, Whytecliffe, Highlands (former) | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Whytecliffe was constructed in 1876 and was designed by prominent Architect F.D.G. Stanley as an elite private residence for Queensland's Crown Solicitor Robert Little'

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Auchenflower takes its name from a house renamed in 1880 by a former Queensland Premier. Which country's estate inspired that name?
bank.reveal: Premier Thomas McIlwraith bought the property in 1880 and named it Auchenflower after his family's estate in Ayrshire, Scotland. The Gaelic name is thought to mean 'field of flowers'.

source.title: Auchenflower | Queensland Places
source.publisher: Centre for the Government of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states McIlwraith 'named it Auchenflower after the McIlwraith family estate in Ayrshire, Scotland' in 1880

bank.prompt: Nyrambla, the grand Ascot mansion that became Australia's WWII code-breaking headquarters, was originally built in 1885–86 as a residence for whom?

options.label: The manager of the Australian Joint Stock Bank

bank.reveal: Nyrambla was built by the Australian Joint Stock Bank in 1885–86 as the residence of its manager, Henry P. Abbott. During WWII, the Central Bureau used it to break Japanese codes.

source.title: Nyrambla | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Nyrambla was built by the Australian Joint Stock Bank in 1885-86 as the residence of its manager, Henry P. Abbott' and that it was 'occupied by the Central Bureau during World War II who worked on breaking Japanese codes'

bank.prompt: Which came first: the first permanent Victoria Bridge over the Brisbane River, or Brisbane's first electric trams?
bank.reveal: The first permanent Victoria Bridge opened in 1874, named by the Governor. Electric trams didn't arrive until 1897 — over two decades later.

source.title: History of Brisbane's Victoria Bridge | State Library of Queensland
source.verifierNote: Page states the permanent Victoria Bridge 'was completed in 1874, opened on 15 June by Governor George Phipps'; trams were introduced in 1897.

bank.prompt: New Farm takes its name from what aspect of the suburb's colonial past?

options.label: A convict-era farm established in the 1830s
A free settler's pastoral run from the 1850s

bank.reveal: The land, known to Indigenous people as 'binkinba', was cleared by convicts for cultivation in the 1830s — making it the settlement's 'new farm' and giving the suburb its name.

source.title: Mossrose Cottage | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'The suburb of New Farm derives its name from its origins as the 'new farm' of the developing convict settlement during the 1830s' and the land 'then known by the indigenous word 'binkinba''.

bank.prompt: When Brisbane City Council renamed West Nundah in 1941, which name was first proposed before the wartime choice was made?
bank.reveal: Plans to develop West Nundah post-war initially proposed 'Beverley Hills', but a more morale-boosting wartime name was chosen — Wavell Heights, after General Archibald Wavell, commander of Allied forces in the Middle East in 1940–41.

source.title: Pfingst Farmhouse | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'Initially it was proposed to change the name of West Nundah to Beverley Hills but due to the war situation, a more morale-boosting name was chosen. This was Wavell Heights and it was named after General Sir Archibald Wavell.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's first tram tracks, laid in 1884, ran between which two points?
bank.reveal: In 1884 the Metropolitan Tramway and Investment Company laid six and a half miles of track from Woolloongabba to Breakfast Creek, with branches to the Exhibition Building and New Farm.

source.title: Tram Shelter | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'In 1884 the privately owned Metropolitan Tramway and Investment Company laid Brisbane's first tram tracks. These covered six and a half miles from Woolloongabba to Breakfast Creek, with branches to the Exhibition Building and New Farm.'

bank.prompt: What was the Kedron district primarily known for before the post-war housing boom turned it into a residential suburb?
bank.reveal: Kedron was 'a farming and tanning district on the outer fringes of suburban Brisbane' — tanneries were active along Kedron Brook — before interwar housing estates and the postwar boom transformed the area.

source.title: Craigie Knowe | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: ''Craigie Knowe' still exists as a reminder of a time when Kedron was a farming and tanning district on the outer fringes of suburban Brisbane.'

bank.prompt: During World War I, what role did the 1880s New Farm mansion 'Strathmore' play from 1916–1918?
bank.reveal: The masonry dwelling at 840 Brunswick Street, New Farm — originally called Strathmore — served as Incholm Private Hospital during World War I from 1916 to 1918, before becoming a boarding house by the late 1930s.

source.title: 840 Brunswick Street, New Farm | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states: 'It served as Incholm Private Hospital during the First World War from 1916-1918, and by the late 1930s was a boarding house.'

Ashgrove State School held its official opening

bank.reveal: The Brisbane Tramway Trust extended the line to Ashgrove in March 1924 — the exact same month the 855-allotment Glenlyon Gardens estate went on sale, acting as the catalyst for Ashgrove's development as a residential suburb.

bank.prompt: The Story Bridge Hotel in Kangaroo Point was NOT always called that. What was it called when it first opened on the same corner around 1878?
bank.reveal: A hotel stood on the corner of Main and Wilson Street from about 1878, known as the Logan Hotel. In 1885 James Darragh rebuilt it and renamed it the Kangaroo Point Hotel — the 'Story Bridge' name came much later.

source.title: Story Bridge Hotel | Heritage Places
source.verifierNote: Page states 'A hotel has been located on the corner of Main and Wilson (now Baildon) Street since circa 1878. The earlier hotel on the site was called the Logan Hotel.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's Old Windmill on Wickham Terrace was built in 1828 — but it almost immediately failed at its one job. What went wrong?

options.label: Its sails never turned in the wind
It ground the wrong type of grain

bank.reveal: The windmill was poorly positioned and its sails failed to catch the breeze, making it useless as a mill. Convicts were put on a treadmill beside it instead to grind grain by foot for up to 14 hours at a time.

source.title: Brisbane City Centre Heritage Place Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'On completion however, the windmill's sails failed to turn' and describes the treadmill as the solution, also confirming it is Queensland's oldest standing building built in 1828.

bank.prompt: The Brisbane suburb of Hamilton got its name in an unusual way. What was it named after?

options.label: Scottish town of Hamilton, home of early settlers

bank.reveal: According to the BCC Ascot and Hamilton Heritage Trail, 'The Hamilton Hotel was established in 1865 and the suburb was subsequently named after it' — making this one of Brisbane's few suburbs named after a pub.

source.title: Ascot and Hamilton Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'The Hamilton Hotel was established in 1865 and the suburb was subsequently named after it.'

bank.prompt: Brisbane's dramatic Kangaroo Point Cliffs are actually man-made. What activity created them?

options.label: Quarrying stone for penal settlement buildings

bank.reveal: Around 1826, Captain Patrick Logan opened a quarry there. 'Brisbane Tuff' stone was cut and punted across the river for penal settlement buildings including the Commissariat Store — the excavation created today's dramatic cliffs.

source.title: Brisbane River Heritage Trail | Brisbane City Council
source.verifierNote: Page states 'Kangaroo Point Cliffs was originally a rocky ridge where, around 1826, Captain Patrick Logan opened a quarry for the penal settlement. It punted stone across the river for government buildings, including the Commissariat Store.'
